proof.title: Proof of one opening
proof.lede: Your browser recomputes this draw from public data. Nothing here depends on trusting the server.
proof.hidden: The result of this draw is shown after the draw ended: the card delivered, or the sale marked as not delivered. Come back in a moment.
proof.provenBody: Every cryptographic rule passed: the card follows from the committed pool, the buyer's seed and the beacon, and the draw key produced the proof.
proof.notProvenBody: At least one rule failed or could not be run. The list below says which.
proof.limits: What this does and does not show
proof.limit1: It shows that the card follows from the committed pool, the buyer's seed, the opening number, the positions already taken and the beacon block, and that the draw key produced the proof. In a chance pack the input also contains the signature of the payment, so it did not exist before the buyer paid. It does not show that the operator delivers: the operator can still move a drawn card away. Such a draw is marked as not delivered, costs the operator a strike and pauses the pack, but Hammerprice cannot refund the buyer.
proof.limit2: In a chance pack the beacon is the first block produced after the payment, so the holder of the draw key cannot compute the result in advance or pick a luckier block, and the buyer cannot know it when paying. In an equal-value pack the beacon is fixed when the pack is published, so it does not show that the key holder did not work results out in advance for seeds somebody told it about.
proof.limit3: The check of the excluded positions uses the public log of this pack. The checks of the beacon block and of the payment need a public node that still has the block and the transaction and are shown as such.
proof.limit4: Equal-value packs only: before you sign, the card is already fixed and is part of the payment. That is harmless there because every card has the same listed value. In a chance pack nothing is chosen before your payment is final: the payment carries no card, and no card appears in any data before it.
proof.limit5: The pool hash freezes the list of cards, not the operator's wallet. If a drawn card has left the operator's wallet, that draw is void: it is marked as not delivered and no second draw is made, so the operator cannot re-roll. Hammerprice holds no money and cannot refund the buyer, who has to claim against the operator. A void or late draw costs the operator a strike and pauses the pack, and the delivery record of every operator is public.

rule.params: The parameters are the committed ones
rule.params_d: Pack, pool hash, buyer, seed, opening number, the excluded positions and, for a chance pack, the payment signature and slot hash to the parameters hash in the input, and the beacon block lies after the payment.
rule.alpha_d: The text that was proven names this network, this request, the parameters hash and the beacon, in the one allowed spelling.
rule.proof_d: The RFC 9381 proof verifies for that input under the draw key.
rule.output: The output is the proof's output
rule.output_d: The output stored for the draw is the one the proof gives.
rule.result: The card follows from the output
rule.result_d: Running the public selection on the output and the pool gives exactly this rarity and card.
rule.taken_d: Every settled earlier card was excluded, and nothing else was excluded except cards that left the pool.
rule.beacon_d: The blockhash of the beacon slot read from the network is the one in the input. For a chance pack it is the first block produced after the payment.
rule.payment_d: Chance packs only: the payment transaction exists on the network, succeeded, landed in the slot the draw names and carries this draw's memo.
rule.order: The draws were made in the order of the payments
rule.order_d: Chance packs only: every earlier draw was paid in an earlier slot, or in the same slot with a smaller transaction id, so the platform did not choose which buyer was drawn first.

manage.title: Your packs
manage.lede: Define a pack of cards you own, publish it, and deliver the sales. In an equal-value pack (every card has the same listed value) you and the buyer sign one transaction. In a chance pack (cards differ in rarity) the buyer pays you directly and first, the card is drawn after the payment is final, and you deliver it with your own signature before the deadline. Hammerprice never holds the money or the cards.
manage.signIn: Sign in with your wallet to manage packs.

manage.oddsHelp: One line per rarity: id, German name, English name, chance in percent. A shorter line works too: id, name, chance (the name then counts for both languages). An equal-value pack has exactly one rarity with the chance 100. A rarity without a card is left out and the others share its chance.
manage.cardsHelp: One line per card: Core asset address, rarity id, name, image URL (https, may stay empty) and the listed value in USDC (the same for every card of an equal-value pack). Separate by a semicolon. An empty rarity id means the first rarity of the odds. You must own every card.

offer.title: How packs work, and how to offer one
offer.lede: A pack is a sealed draw from a pool of real cards. If you own the cards, you can define a pack, publish it and sell it. Buyers pay you directly.

steps.cards: You pick cards you own: the Metaplex Core assets in your wallet.
steps.tiers: You set 1 to 8 tiers (rarities), the odds per tier (together 100 percent) and a price in USDC.
steps.public: The odds, the whole pool and a commitment hash are public before any sale and appear on the pack page. After you publish, nothing can be edited; you can only pause, resume or close the pack.
steps.value: A card value you list is your own figure, never a promise. A buyer can receive a card worth more or less than the price.
steps.pay: The buyer pays you directly, and first. Hammerprice only takes its fee in the same payment.
steps.deliver: After the payment is final, a card is drawn by a public random draw. You must deliver that card within the deadline (24 hours after the draw by default). If it passes or you move the drawn card away, the sale counts as not delivered, you get a strike (20 strikes suspend you) and the pack is paused.
steps.record: Every seller has a public delivery record: delivered, late, not delivered and the median time to deliver.
steps.custody: Hammerprice holds no pool, no money and no cards, so it cannot refund a buyer. Keep the pool cards in your wallet. Buyers should check the seller's record before paying and keep the payment and the proof.
steps.adults: Buyers must confirm that they are 18 or older.

offer.sellBody: Instead of one card in a room, put several of your cards into a pack with published odds. Buyers pay you directly and you deliver the drawn card.

sections.delivery: Payment and delivery: no pool at Hammerprice

odds.p1: Each tier has odds in basis points (one hundredth of a percent), and all tiers together add up to 10,000. They are hashed into the pool hash before the first sale, so the odds you see are the odds that are used.
odds.p2: The draw turns the ECVRF output into a fair whole number from 0 up to one less than the total, which is 0 to 9,999 while every tier still has a card. The tiers are walked in the published order, and the tier whose range contains the number is the one drawn. Then one card of that tier is picked the same fair way: every card of the tier that is still free is equally likely.
odds.p3: If a tier has no free card left, it drops out of that draw and the other tiers share its weight in proportion. Nothing else influences the result. Anyone can recompute any draw on its proof page, /verify/packs/ followed by the draw id.
odds.example: Example: Common 7,000, Rare 2,500, Chase 500. Common covers 0 to 6,999, Rare 7,000 to 9,499 and Chase 9,500 to 9,999. The number 9,612 is a Chase. If the Chase tier holds 2 cards, each of them has half of that 5 percent, so 2.5 percent.

notice.chance: 18+. Your counterparty is the seller {seller} ({record}). The card must be delivered within 24 hours of the draw by default; otherwise there is no card, and Hammerprice, which never holds your payment, cannot refund you. Odds and pool are public.
